questions.enonce_markdown: List the parts of the mammalian eye. *(9 marks)*
Describe the function of the eye in image formation. *(6 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. Light rays from an object **enter the eye through the cornea**, which does most of the **refraction (bending)** of light.
2. The light passes through the **aqueous humour** and the **pupil**; the **iris** adjusts the size of the pupil to control the amount of light entering the eye.
3. The light then passes through the **lens**, which **refracts it further** and **focuses it**, and through the **vitreous humour**.
4. A **real, inverted and diminished image** is formed on the **retina**, particularly at the yellow spot (fovea).
5. The **rods and cones** of the retina are **stimulated**; rods respond to dim light and cones to bright light and colour. They send **nerve impulses** along the **optic nerve** to the brain.
6. The **brain (visual centre of the cerebrum)** interprets the impulses and the image is **seen the right way up**.

questions.enonce_markdown: How is the eye adapted to viewing far objects? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
To view a **far (distant) object**, the eye **accommodates** as follows:

1. The **ciliary muscles relax**.
2. The **suspensory ligaments are pulled tight (they become taut)**, because the pressure of the eyeball pulls on them.
3. The **lens is pulled thin (flattened) and becomes less convex**.
4. The lens therefore has a **longer focal length** and refracts light **less**.
5. The nearly parallel rays coming from the distant object are **focused sharply on the retina**, so the image is clear.
